subject: Re: Scale breakpoints, SLA tradeoffs & crediting structure
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Inbound: volume breakpoints + SLAs

Hi Marcus,

Quick intro — I lead platform infra at BrightCart. We’re running a multi-region recommendation system and expect token consumption to spike Q4. We like Redwood’s batching and fallback routing, but procurement needs clarity on:

- Baseline hosted API pricing at scale (100M - 1B tokens/month)
- Exact breakpoints where unit price steps down
- What SLA tiers (latency/availability) are tied to different pricing bands
- Whether unused reserved credits can roll or be converted into support/observability credits

Can you share a clean rate card and note any flexibility for an initial 12-month commitment? I can loop in procurement if you need to see an internal forecast.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Director, Platform Engineering, BrightCart
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightcart.com>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Inbound: volume breakpoints + SLAs

Hi Samir — great to meet you. I’ve attached our August rate card and a short usage-scenario worksheet to help map breakpoints to your forecast. Key points up front:

- Baseline (hosted API): $0.0016 per 1K completion tokens / $0.0012 per 1K prompt tokens.
- Volume discounts (prescriptive bands):
  * 0–100M tokens/mo: baseline rates (no discount)
  * 100M–500M tokens/mo: 12% off baseline unit rates
  * 500M–1B tokens/mo: 24% off baseline unit rates
  * 1B+ tokens/mo: bespoke pricing (typically 30–45% off baseline with SLA commit)
- SLA tie-ins: the 500M+ bands unlock SLA-backed latency targets (p99 < 800ms for common prompt sizes) and 99.95% availability. Lower bands get standard best-effort latency guidance.
- Credit rules: unused monthly credits can be banked up to 3 months or converted (on a 1:1 value basis) into Redwood Console retention and advanced tracing credits, subject to annual commit.

I attached: redwood_ratecard_aug2026.pdf and a quick brightcart_usage_estimate.xlsx that I filled from the numbers you mentioned. If you want, I can put together two scenarios: a) a conservative 12-month commit (starts 100M/mo growth to 500M) and b) an aggressive ramp (starts 300M -> 1B).

Are you available for a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the breakpoints and SLA tradeoffs? If procurement wants to see contract language we can surface a standard SOW + commitment appendix.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_ratecard_aug2026.pdf (pdf)]
[attachment: brightcart_usage_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: BrightCart: volume breakpoints + SLA questions — request for approval

Ben / Evelyn / Laura — forwarding Samir's note and the attached estimate. BrightCart looks like a credible mid-market scale deal: initial ask is clarity on banded pricing for up to ~1B tokens. Two asks from me:

1) Can we offer the 500M–1B band at 26% off baseline unit rates (vs. standard 24%) if BrightCart signs a 12-month 750M/mo commit with flexible burst?
2) Can we allow banking of unused credits up to 6 weeks (instead of standard 3 months) but provide an option to convert leftover credits into Console retention credits at 1:1? Procurement will push for carry-forward; we should keep some guardrails.

Evelyn — can you confirm the latency SLO language we should commit to for the 500M band (I proposed p99 < 800ms) and any guardrails on prompt length distribution?
Laura — need a quick look at the proposed discount and conversion flow from accounting/finance side. Does a 26% effective discount at 750M/mo look acceptable under current margin targets?

Thanks,
Marcus

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 11:30 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [see original to Samir with attachments]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightCart: volume breakpoints + SLA questions — request for approval

Marcus — good ask. I’m comfortable with a customer-facing offer along these lines with two conditions:

- Condition A: The 26% band is a time-limited introductory incentive for the first 6 months of the commit; after that we revert to standard 24% unless they agree to a stepped higher commit. This protects margin vs. unknown churn.
- Condition B: Banking window can be 2 months (60 days). If BrightCart routinely exceeds banking, we’ll move them to a higher guaranteed minimum or require forecasting cadence.

Evelyn — confirm SLO language. Laura — if 26% over 6 months still holds margin targets given the estimated usage, we sign off.

Ben
VP, Commercials
[signature redwood.ai]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightcart.com>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 18:10:00 -0400
Subject: Final proposal: 12-month commit — pricing & next steps

Hi Samir — thanks for the call last week. Based on your Q4 ramp and the internal approvals, here’s a concise proposal for a 12-month engaged commitment:

Offer summary (12-month, starts Sept 1):
- Commit: 750M tokens/month guaranteed
- Rate: 26% off baseline unit pricing for the first 6 months, reverting to 24% thereafter unless you elect to extend/re-step the commit
- SLA: 500M+ band SLA applied — p99 latency target < 800ms for 0–1024 token requests; 99.95% availability across primary region with cross-region fallback; incident credits per contract appendix
- Banking: unused committed credits may be banked up to 60 days. Unused credits beyond banking window may be converted into Console retention/tracing credits at 1:1 value (opt-in during signing).
- Add-ons: optional advanced tracing retention (extra fee) — we can include as a line item in the SOW.

Attachments: redwood_ratecard_aug2026.pdf, brightcart_usage_estimate.xlsx
Contract steps:
1) I’ll send a DocuSign with the SOW + commitment appendix (link here: https://docsend.com/view/rc-redwood-proposal-aug2026).
2) Procurement review (we’re open to a short review period + a single redline cycle).
3) Kickoff with solutions engineering and an initial workshop to lock down prompt distributions and batching settings.

If that works, can procurement confirm a target signature date by Aug 31 so we can provision reserved capacity ahead of your Q4 ramp?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
